function: Learns jointly the RIS phase-shifts, NOMA user pairing and satellite power allocation to maximize the average sum rate of a RIS-assisted NOMA satellite downlink (pp. 1, 3).
system: Satellite and 8 ground users with 1×1 direct links (single antenna), 4 NOMA pairs; reflecting RIS, 10 to 50 elements; 1 GHz bandwidth, carrier unstated (pp. 2, 4, 5).
method: PPO-DQN: PPO actor-critic for continuous phase shifts and power ratio, DQN for discrete user pairing; deep reinforcement learning trained by interaction with the environment (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Own simulated channels: Rician for satellite-RIS and RIS-user links, Rayleigh for satellite-user link, with path-loss exponents; fixed geometry; no standard model, dataset or measurement (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: One simulated setup with fixed positions; no separate test set; Figs. 3-4 sweep RIS elements (10-50) and bandwidth (0.6-1 GHz), unclear whether retrained (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Four own schemes: PPO-DQN with random power; random RIS phases; no RIS with near-far pairing and PPO power; sequential DQN then PPO. No earlier published method (p. 4).
metrics: Average sum rate (Figs. 3-4) and cumulative reward during training (Fig. 2) (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "follows Rayleigh fading" for the satellite-user link, with Rician factors for the other two links (eqs. 2-4); own LoS plus NLoS simulator, no 3GPP model, dataset or measurement is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 5: "Impact of reflection elements on the average sum rate" (Fig. 3, and Fig. 4 for bandwidth) are sweeps of system parameters; the paper never states that a trained agent is tested on unseen conditions, and the PPO action space has (B + K) dimensions (p. 3), so another B implies another agent.
q3_support: p. 5: "other schemes only consider parts of optimization variables" or use DRL independently per variable type; Schemes 2, 3 and 5 (p. 4) are ablations or a sequential DQN-then-PPO variant of the proposed method, so there is no earlier published learned method nor a standard DRL algorithm on the full problem; non-learned baselines exist (random RIS, near-far pairing).
q4_support: p. 1: "algorithm has high complexity" refers to the alternating optimization of prior work [4], not to PPO-DQN; no order, operations, parameters or runtime of the proposed method is reported, and p. 4 lists only learning rates, discount factors and batch size.
q5_support: p. 4: "The simulation parameters are" listed for the authors' own simulator; no code or data link, no public dataset and no availability statement appear on pp. 1-5.
notes: Included in area 6: learned PPO-DQN control of RIS phases and satellite power plus NOMA pairing on a satellite link; area 6 outranks 3 by the specificity order. Borderline q3: Scheme 5 (sequential DQN then PPO, p. 4) was treated as the proposed method trained in another way, so no independent learned baseline; the reviewer may confirm. The paper prints Rylance for Rician (p. 2). Fig. 2 title gives K = 8, M = 40, power 15 W; Figs. 3-4 use total power 60 W.
